items.title: Liquid AI releases d1.3-ultra decision model, tied for first on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index
items.summary: Liquid's d1.3-ultra update adds ranking and top-k selection, number and date extraction, and audio span extraction, and is trained to treat planted instructions in inputs as data. Artificial Analysis independently scores it 76 on its Decision Index v2.1, tied with Bison 31B at about 60% lower cost per million tasks.

reception.summary: Replies are mostly short, generic praise about audio span extraction; one user could not find it in the Liquid Console and asked whether it is US-only, another asked for OpenRouter.

items.title: Google Antigravity release cuts Auto-mode approvals another 15% and adds native GitHub PR pills
items.summary: The day-after-Thanksgiving Antigravity release trims unnecessary approvals in Auto mode by a further 15% and adds native GitHub integration: paste a PR link into chat to reference it inline, hover for status, branches and comments, and see all linked PRs in the Overview menu.

reception.summary: Few replies discuss the feature; most ask about weekly usage limits running out, bans for using other harnesses, proxy settings, and Auto mode missing on Windows 10.

items.title: Strata 0.2.23 adds GSQ-RCO IQ3_S and four other Inkling 2 Mini builds plus up to 64 parallel requests
items.summary: The MIT-licensed Strata local engine now ships five Inkling 2 Mini builds from 10.5 to 19.4 GB, including the GSQ-RCO IQ3_S quant, fixes long-context regressions and serves up to 64 parallel requests, so the 26B looped MoE runs faster on consumer GPUs.

items.title: NVIDIA Research Test-time Baking keeps novel-view rendering fast as more photos are added
items.summary: Test-time Baking trains a compact network to imitate how a multi-view model combines information across input photos, so rendering new viewpoints stays fast while quality stays close to the original model as photo count grows. Paper, code, weights and a demo are out for the NeurIPS 2026 spotlight.

items.title: Training-free looped transformer: rerunning 3 layers of frozen Qwen3-0.6B raises ARC-Easy accuracy
items.summary: A Hugging Face engineer reproduces the Training-Free Looped Transformers paper by running three layers of a frozen Qwen3-0.6B twice at half a step per pass, raising ARC-Easy accuracy with no weight changes; code and eval results are in a Hugging Face bucket.

doubt.pushback: A replier notes the paper's best 0.6B method (heavy-ball) gains only 0.13 points on ARC-Easy in the posted results.json, and others ask for the baseline and the extra compute and KV-cache cost.

reception.summary: Mostly interested builders planning to try it; specific questions about KV cache handling in decoding, compute overhead, the small heavy-ball gain, and whether longer CoT does the same.

items.title: SGLang makes Intel Xeon CPUs and Intel GPUs first-class serving platforms
items.summary: SGLang now serves on Intel Xeon with AMX compute, W8A8 INT8 and NUMA-aware threads, and on Intel GPUs with native XPU attention and grouped MoE kernels, speculative decoding and graph capture; MXFP4 MoE on Xe2 keeps expert weights packed in device memory.

items.title: Physical Intelligence Index ranks robot models by blind head-to-head Elo on real robots
items.summary: RoboColosseum's new weekly index ranks robot policies, world action models and LLM agents by Elo from 27,688 blind head-to-head trials on real robots; Dream-1, GPT-6.2 Astra and Fable 5.2 lead, with MolmoAct2 the best VLA at eighth.

doubt.pushback: The post itself notes the leaders are thinly tested at about 400 to 600 comparisons each, against about 4,000 for VLAs, so top ranks may move.

items.title: omarchy-mlx brings Linux MLX inference on Apple Silicon to parity with macOS
items.summary: On Linux on Apple Silicon, omarchy-mlx now runs Qwen3.8-2B at 215 tok/s on an M2 Max (213 on macOS) and Qwen3-4B at 105 tok/s on an M1 Max (104 on macOS); a fix for slow M5 Max runs is up for testing. MIT repo.

doubt.pushback: The margins are about 1%, within run-to-run noise, so this is parity rather than a clear win; the post also promotes a hardware wishlist.

items.title: 10 MB page-script classifiers route scanned PDFs to the right OCR pipeline at 1,773 pages/s
items.summary: Two tiny image classifiers trained for $25.50 on Hugging Face Jobs predict which of 21 writing scripts a page uses, at 11 ms on CPU or 1,773 pages/s on an A10G, so web-scale PDF crawls can be pre-sorted before paying for OCR; a run over 21,490 Common Crawl pages cost 18 cents.

items.title: TRL async GRPO now powers RL for genomic models, a 2B olympiad prover and multi-harness coding agents
items.summary: Hugging Face TRL's asynchronous RL trainer is the base for the RL stage of the Carbon-X genomic model, a 2B proof-writing model in FineEnvs, coding agents from 1.7B to 27B trained inside pi, OpenCode and Hermes, and the async RL in Unsloth, Axolotl and Snowflake Arctic Platform.

items.title: HyperHarness trains one generator that writes a personalized agent harness from each user's history
items.summary: A Microsoft-led paper trains a single generator that, given a user's history, has an LLM write that user's retrieval and answer-guidance functions, refined by task scores across training users, so personalized assistants adapt per user without per-user search or updating the answering model.
